title: Learning Boltzmann Generators via Constrained Mass Transport
claim: Existing annealing schedules either teleport mass or lose overlap with the start; combining both constraints keeps successive densities overlapping and smooth.
layout: 4 panels left-to-right, stacked ridgeline densities top to bottom, ours rightmost
description: Four side-by-side ridgeline plots, each titled with an annealing path type: Geometric AP with a linear schedule, Geometric AP via (2), Tempered AP via (7), and Geometric-tempered AP via (9). Each panel stacks about ten 1-D densities in shades of blue, from light at the top (initial broad q0) to dark at the bottom (bimodal target p). In the linear and geometric panels, mass piles up on one mode and the second mode suddenly appears later, which shows teleportation. In the tempered panel, both modes are present early but the density never overlaps q0. In the rightmost panel, the density moves smoothly from q0 and both modes grow together. The eye goes first to the titles, then to the progression of the dark ridges at the bottom of each panel.
caption: Illustration of the annealing paths (AP) obtained by solving the variational problems [ref], [ref], or [ref]. Trust-region–based optimization [ref] mitigates the irregularities of naive schedules (e.g., the linear schedule), but the resulting geometric AP suffers from mass teleportation as the right mode of the target distribution $p$ emerges without overlap with earlier intermediate densities. Constraining the entropy decay between successive densities [ref] prevents mass teleportation, yet fails to guarantee sufficient overlap between the initial distribution $q_0$ and subsequent intermediate densities. In contrast, combining both constraints [ref] yields APs that both maintain overlap between successive densities and avoid mass teleportation.
abstract: Efficient sampling from high-dimensional and multimodal unnormalized probability distributions is a central challenge in many areas of science and machine learning. We focus on Boltzmann generators (BGs) that aim to sample the Boltzmann distribution of physical systems, such as molecules, at a given temperature. Classical variational approaches that minimize the reverse Kullback-Leibler divergence are prone to mode collapse, while annealing-based methods, commonly using geometric schedules, can suffer from mass teleportation and rely heavily on schedule tuning. We introduce Constrained Mass Transport (CMT), a variational framework that generates intermediate distributions under constraints on both the KL divergence and the entropy decay between successive steps. These constraints enhance distributional overlap, mitigate mass teleportation, and counteract premature convergence. Across standard BG benchmarks and the here introduced ELIL tetrapeptide, the largest system studied to date without access to samples from molecular dynamics, CMT consistently surpasses state-of-the-art variational methods, achieving more than 2.5x higher effective sample size while avoiding mode collapse.
